sources.title: Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (author-hosted draft)
sources.locator: Theorem 5.2.11 and proof, printed pp.221–222; §5.4 Theorem 5.4.1, Corollary 5.4.2 and Lemma 5.4.7, pp.230–235; §5.5 Theorem 5.5.1 and Lemma 5.5.2, pp.237–239; Example 5.6.10, pp.246–248; Example 6.1.3(2), pp.249–250

contents.name: Theorem 5.2.11(1), invariant Hermitian form defined by normalized Haar averaging
contents.support: The local definition fixes the first-variable-linear convention and writes the normalized scalar integral explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2.11(1), finite-dimensional compact representation splits into irreducibles
contents.support: The local proof spells out invariant orthogonal complements and finite induction, including the zero-dimensional case.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2.11(1), compact averaging gives invariant positive Hermitian form and finite-dimensional semisimplicity
Theorem 5.2.11(2), Hilbert-space unitarization under bounded-operator hypotheses
contents.reason: General unitarization of bounded Hilbert-space representations is stronger than the finite-dimensional assertion and is not used by any RG-21 item.

contents.name: Example 5.2.12, SU(2) polynomial-representation invariant form
contents.reason: This compact-Lie polynomial model belongs to the existing compact-Lie development; this pair uses the circle to illustrate the averaging mechanism.

contents.name: Theorem 5.4.1, Peter–Weyl decomposition of the regular representation
contents.reason: Density and the full regular Hilbert decomposition are assigned to RG-22; using them for RG-21 finite-dimensionality would reverse the planned proof order.

contents.name: Theorem 5.4.1 proof, convolution kernel f(xy−1) is Hilbert–Schmidt
contents.support: Only convolution on L²(K) is covered; the arbitrary-irreducible argument uses rank-one averaging instead.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4.2(1), compact irreducible unitary representations are finite dimensional
contents.support: Conclusion retained; source proof depends on Peter–Weyl, so the local proof uses the independent rank-one route.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4.2(2) and Lemma 5.4.7, every unitary representation decomposes into irreducibles
contents.reason: The arbitrary Hilbert direct-sum decomposition needs density of compact spectral pieces and is expressly owned by RG-22, not this preliminary projection page.

contents.name: Lemma 5.5.2, orthogonality and dimension normalization of matrix coefficients
contents.support: The local proof uses direct Haar averaging of a rank-one operator, avoiding the source’s preceding Peter–Weyl decomposition.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.1(2), character integral defining an isotypic projection
contents.support: The theorem displays the character integral and dimension factor; the local definition spells out the conjugate-character convention under first-variable-linear inner products and strong Bochner integration.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.1(2), character formula for an isotypic projection
contents.support: Formula and normalization retained; local proof establishes range and idempotence before any Peter–Weyl density theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.1(1), characters form a complete orthonormal basis of class functions
contents.reason: Completeness of the class-function basis is a Peter–Weyl consequence and is not needed for the pair’s individual isotypic projections.

contents.name: Example 5.6.10, irreducibles and coefficient density for infinite products
contents.reason: The classification and density of irreducibles of infinite compact products require the later Peter–Weyl argument; RG-21 uses only the no-faithful-finite-dimensional boundary example.

contents.name: Example 6.1.3(2), infinite product of nontrivial compact groups has no faithful finite-dimensional representation
contents.support: The local countable C₂ product proof uses an elementary no-small-involutions argument and a direct choice-free binary-tree compactness proof.

read_verification.method: Downloaded the complete 338-page PDF, extracted text with mutool, and inspected the named statements and relevant complete proofs at the listed printed pages. Its Corollary 5.4.2 proof uses Peter–Weyl and is not this page’s proof route.

sources.title: Vera Serganova, Representation Theory lecture notes, Chapter III
sources.locator: Chapter III §1.6 Proposition 1.23 through Lemma 1.30, printed pp.55–57; §2.1 Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Corollary 2.7 and Exercise 2.10, printed pp.57–60

contents.name: Proposition 1.23, rank-one averaging construction in its irreducible-representation proof
contents.support: The proof begins with an irreducible representation; this page uses only that case, not the proposition’s broader wording.

contents.name: Exercise 1.24, averaged rank-one operator is compact positive and intertwining
contents.support: The source poses positivity, compactness and intertwining as an exercise; the local proof supplies the missing finite-rank norm-continuity and Bochner norm-limit arguments.

contents.name: Corollary 1.25, compact-group irreducible unitary representations are finite dimensional
Lemma 1.26, irreducibles embed into the regular representation
contents.reason: Embedding arbitrary irreducibles into the regular representation is a Peter–Weyl interface and is not used to prove RG-21 finite-dimensionality.

contents.name: Theorem 1.29, orthogonal complement of a closed invariant subspace is invariant
Lemma 1.30, dense semisimple submodule of arbitrary unitary representation
contents.reason: Density of all irreducible pieces and the global Hilbert direct-sum statement belong to RG-22; the source’s broader Proposition 1.23 proof is insufficient for this use as written.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1, compact Schur orthogonality by averaging rank-one maps
Corollary 2.2, irreducible characters are orthonormal
Corollary 2.7, Peter–Weyl L² decomposition
contents.reason: The complete L² direct sum is explicitly the next RG-22 A-page result and must not be imported into the preliminary projection proof.

contents.name: Exercise 2.10, isotypic projection with printed 1/d prefactor
contents.reason: The printed 1/d prefactor contradicts the normalized Haar character calculation for d>1; the correct d prefactor is taken from Kowalski and Vogan and proved locally.

read_verification.method: Downloaded complete 159-page PDF, extracted text with mutool, and inspected the rank-one averaging, finite-dimensionality, orthogonality and projection passages. The proof of Proposition 1.23 starts with an irreducible representation despite a broader heading; Exercise 2.10 prints an inconsistent 1/d factor.

sources.title: David Vogan, Review of Harmonic Analysis on Compact Groups
sources.locator: Complete 12-page note, especially Definition 2.1, formulas (2.5)–(2.9), Theorem 2.13(4), Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17

contents.name: Definition 2.1, compact finite-dimensional representations and intertwiners
contents.support: Finite-dimensional intertwiner setting motivates the general weak operator average, whose existence is proved locally.

contents.name: Formula (2.5), compact convolution by Haar integration
Theorem 2.6, Fourier transform turns convolution into multiplication
contents.reason: The operator-valued Fourier transform algebra is part of RG-22 general compact harmonic analysis, not needed for the RG-21 Hilbert–Schmidt kernel argument.

contents.name: Formulas (2.7)–(2.9), left/right translations and matrix coefficients
contents.support: Translate the source’s inverse-on-group coefficient convention before applying the rank-one calculation.

contents.name: Proposition 2.8, Fourier transform respects translations
contents.reason: Full Fourier-transform covariance on measures belongs with the RG-22 Fourier and Peter–Weyl construction; RG-21 uses only elementary Haar change of variables.

contents.name: Definition 2.10 and Proposition 2.11, inverse transform and coefficient span
contents.reason: Representative-function and inverse-Fourier-transform structure is an RG-22 topic; no inverse transform is needed for a single isotypic projector.

contents.name: Theorem 2.13(4), Schur coefficient normalization Vol(K)/dim σ
contents.support: For normalized Haar, Vol(K)=1, yielding 1/dim σ. The local proof uses rank-one averaging directly.

contents.name: Theorem 2.13(1–3), Peter–Weyl isomorphisms on K-finite functions and measures
contents.reason: Surjectivity and the K-finite Fourier isomorphisms belong to the later Peter–Weyl page; they are not prerequisites for RG-21 projections.

contents.name: Corollary 2.16, character formula with dim σ/Vol(K) projection normalization
contents.support: With normalized Haar, the correct multiplier is dim σ; local proof establishes the projector properties without using Theorem 2.13 surjectivity.

contents.name: Proposition 2.17, transpose identity for Fourier and inverse Fourier transforms
contents.reason: The transpose duality of the operator-valued Fourier transform is beyond the local averaging and projection assertions required on RG-21.

read_verification.method: Downloaded the complete 12-page PostScript, converted it to PDF with ps2pdf, extracted text with mutool, and inspected the displayed calculations and proof through Corollary 2.16. The source uses inverse matrix-coefficient convention; formulas were translated to this track’s first-variable-linear convention.

sources.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendix A
sources.locator: Appendix A §A.5, Proposition A.5.1 and Theorem A.5.2, printed pp.323–324 in the fetched edition

contents.name: Proposition A.5.1, a locally compact group has finite Haar measure exactly when compact
contents.support: Specialized to R; the local proof gives explicit disjoint translated intervals.

contents.name: Theorem A.5.2(ii), compact irreducible unitary representations are finite dimensional
contents.support: Statement corroboration only; the source refers to Peter–Weyl and does not supply the local rank-one proof.

contents.name: Theorem A.5.2(i,iii), arbitrary unitary direct sums and regular-representation multiplicities
contents.reason: The full discrete decomposition and regular multiplicity statement are Peter–Weyl results assigned to RG-22; they are not used to prove RG-21.

read_verification.method: Downloaded the complete 523-page PDF, extracted text with mutool, and inspected Appendix A §A.5 including the full Proposition A.5.1 argument and Theorem A.5.2 statement. The theorem is quoted there without a proof, so rank-one proof support comes from Serganova.
